lead.hed: USNI: Hormuz tanker transits rose more than 30 percent last week
lead.insight: USNI News, Friday evening: transits through the Strait of Hormuz rose more than 30 percent last week, led mostly by tankers and gas carriers. Lloyd’s List Intelligence counted 114 transits between Aug. 17 and Sunday, compared with the Aug. 10–16 week. The count is still below pre-war levels and is likely to move as more dark tankers are identified. The item is a weekly traffic tally, not a Navy declaration that the strait is open.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 1st Class Indra Beaufort · DVIDS 9441586 · PUBLIC DOMAIN · Quartermaster 1st Class Richard Williams uses a sextant aboard USS Roosevelt (DDG 80) during a Strait of Hormuz transit. Date taken Dec. 13, 2025. Caption must say December file photo, not this week’s tanker count.
lead.image_note: Official U.S. Navy DVIDS still of a Hormuz transit aboard USS Roosevelt. Same-subject class as Friday’s tanker-transit tally — not the recycled Arabian Sea formation still, not an F-15, not a brand tile.

political.hed: USNI: Abraham Lincoln entered the Malacca Strait on Friday
political.insight: USNI’s Western Pacific Pulse, Friday: USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) entered the north end of the Malacca Strait on Friday, according to automatic identification system data. The Pulse is a weekly ship-movement summary. The Navy did not publish a next port in that item.

political.hed: Navy accepts the last Expeditionary Sea Base, named for a Marine
political.insight: Navy press release, Wednesday: the service accepted delivery of USNS Hector A. Cafferata Jr. (ESB 8) from General Dynamics NASSCO in San Diego on Aug. 25, after integrated sea trials this summer. The ship honors Marine Pfc. Hector A. Cafferata Jr., Medal of Honor at Chosin Reservoir. It is the sixth and final ESB. The Navy has not named an operating area.

political.hed: USNI: Navy wants a standoff aerial torpedo for carrier aircraft
political.insight: USNI, Friday: the Navy is looking to develop a next-generation standoff torpedo that can be carried by carrier-based aircraft and drones. Naval Air Systems Command released a request for information Tuesday on the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo. An RFI is a market survey, not a production buy.

tech.hed: OpenAI letter: a limited window to strengthen cyber defense
tech.insight: OpenAI published an open letter Thursday calling for collective action on cyber defense as AI-enabled attacks get cheaper. CNBC counted 116 companies and entities on the roster, including Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and AMD. The letter asks governments to fund defense for hospitals and water plants. It is a joint appeal, not a statute.

tech.hed: CISA’s NetScaler patch deadline for federal agencies is today
tech.insight: CISA on Wednesday added six flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including CVE-2026-8452 in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway. Binding Operational Directive 26-04 tells federal civilian agencies to remediate listed high-risk holes on publicly exposed assets. SecurityWeek reported the federal due date as Aug. 29. CISA encourages other operators to treat the catalog the same way; the directive itself binds federal agencies.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty: Kafka’s court still maps how scapegoats are made
culture.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: Daniel H. Burns reads The Trial as a picture of justice that starts blindfolded, grows wings as activism, and ends as the hunt. He argues online antisemitism now skips the legal costume and sells bloodlust as entertainment. The essay is a reading of Kafka, not a crime blotter.

watch.hed: WATCH: Air Force F-15 ceiling is $131 billion, not a jet on signing
watch.insight: Defense News, Friday: the Air Force awarded Boeing a sole-source F-15 Eagle Crest contract with a $131.23 billion ceiling through 2037. The Aug. 24 notice obligated $343,740 in fiscal 2026 research money at award. Friday’s lead; Saturday’s board keeps the ceiling on Watch.
